chunks: If it is said: What do you mean by empowering him?
Do you mean that we find him and converse with him, and that is not possible except with his existence.
It was said to you: None of that is valid except with his manifestation and our knowledge, or the knowledge of some of us, of his place.

And if you say: We mean by empowering him that we submit to his obedience and strengthen his hand, and refrain from helping the tyrants, and stand to support him whenever he calls us to his Imamate and indicates it to us through his miracle.

We said to you: Then we can do that during the time of occultation, even if the Imam is not present in it, so how do you say that what we are ordained to do cannot be performed except with the presence of the Imam.

We said: What we say in this matter is what Murtadha (may God have mercy on him) mentioned in Al-Dhakhira and what we mentioned in Talkhis Al-Shafi, that which is our grace from the Imam's action and the extension of his hand, is not complete except by three matters.
ai.seo_question: How can Muslims obey and support the Imam during his occultation if he is not physically present?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* refutes the objection that obedience (*ta'ah*) and support (*ansar*) require the Imam's physical presence by distinguishing between the general authority of the Imam and the specific spiritual grace (*lutf*) that is contingent upon his existence. It cites the scholar al-Murtada to establish that while certain acts of devotion can be performed during the Minor and Major Occultation, the full realization of divine benevolence through the Imam's influence remains tied to his actual presence, thereby clarifying the theological boundaries of the occultation period.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Objection: What do you mean by saying that we should empower him?
Do you mean that we find him and converse with him?
Reply: That is not possible without him being existent.
You will be told that none of that is possible without him being manifest and without us knowing, or someone of us knowing his place.

If you say, “We mean by empowering him that we should submit to his obedience, fight under his command, refrain from helping the tyrants and rise to his support when he calls us to his Imamate and proves it to us through his miracles,” we will say to you it is possible for us to do that during occultation, even if it is a time without an Imam. How do you say then what we have been ordained to do cannot be performed without an Imam?
Our response here is what Murtadha has mentioned in Dhakhira and what we have mentioned in Talkhis Shafi.
